findings.title: No online way to change or cancel an existing booking
findings.description: Changing the slot of an existing booking is a top task, but once a booking is made no route accepts a reference to change or cancel it. The done page offers only 'Book another slot' and 'If you cannot come, call 01632 960771 on a weekday'. The phone line is open weekdays 09:00 to 17:00, but residents mostly book in the evening and visit at weekends.
findings.impact: Residents changing a booking ('move it to the afternoon') on a Friday evening or at the weekend cannot do so. They may book a second slot (households are limited to two a week) or simply not turn up, which leaves a scarce slot unused.

findings.title: Selected day and vehicle are marked only by a faint tint, weaker than unselected outlines
findings.description: The chosen day (Saturday 17) and the chosen vehicle (Van) get a very pale green fill and a slightly darker border, while every unselected option already has a bold green or dark outline. At 375 slot-chosen, 'Tomorrow' and 'Saturday 17' both appear tinted.
findings.impact: Day and vehicle are the two choices that decide whether the resident is let in.

harm.statement: A resident on a phone may not be sure which day or vehicle is chosen, and may book the wrong day or vehicle without noticing.

evidence.detail: Tomorrow and Saturday 17 both tinted; difference barely visible

findings.recommendation: Give the selected state of choice buttons a treatment that is stronger than the resting outline and unmistakable at phone size; check the Tomorrow tint is not a stray state.

verification_check.reason: Partly a harness artefact, and the harm is not shown. For days the selected border is thicker, not weaker. The chosen day is also restated in the 'Saturday 17 October' caption, in the slot count and in 'Your booking' on the confirm page, so the claim that a resident could book the wrong day without noticing is not supported.

findings.title: No identity or focal point of the recycling centre on any screen (sterile default)
findings.description: Every screen is a heading, a step line and bordered boxes on a pale ground; the only identity is 'Dunmore District Council' and a 1.5px bin icon in the masthead. Nothing from the centre's world (Quarry Road, the gate, the waste streams residents sort into) is drawn on, and no element would be missed if moved to another council form.
findings.impact: Brand pair 'plain, not bare' drifts to bare; the identity floor that Operate surfaces still need is missing.
findings.recommendation: Decide one element taken from the centre's own mechanism (the gate check, the reference, the waste streams) that can recur quietly across the four steps without breaking Operate conventions.

findings.title: Wide widths leave the right half of the page empty while cards stretch with text in their left half
findings.description: At 1280 and 1440 the slot grid stops at about 820px and form columns at about 610px inside a 1184px container, while 'Opening days', 'Your booking' and 'Your reference' cards stretch full width with their text in the left half.
findings.impact: Desktop pages look unfinished and unbalanced; a design note, not a task harm.
findings.recommendation: Decide one content width per step and make cards and controls share it.

findings.title: Narrow-width wraps split the registration example and strand words
findings.description: At 320 the confirm hint and error break 'AB12 / CDE' across lines, and 'it.' sits alone on the last line of the 'Nothing is paid' note; at 375 the footer phone number breaks '01632 / 960771'.
findings.impact: Small finish lapses on the phone widths most residents use; design note.
findings.recommendation: Keep registrations and phone numbers unbroken and balance short final lines.

findings.title: No identity or signature: 'plain' has become 'bare'
findings.description: Across all four steps the only identity is 'Dunmore District Council' in bold body sans with a small bin glyph. No element comes from the centre's world (the gate, the bays, the permit, the reference read at the gate). DESIGN.md declares 'plain, not bare'.
findings.impact: Design note: the service reads as a default form and the brand pair's Y side is what shows.
findings.recommendation: Choose one element from the centre's own mechanism (most naturally the reference shown at the gate) and give it a treatment that carries 'plain, not bare' on every step.

findings.title: Done page at wide widths: stretched card, half-width card, band under footer
findings.description: At 1280 the reference card spans the full content width with its text in the left half, the 'At the centre' card stops at half width, and the page ends with an empty grey band below the white footer.
findings.impact: Design note: the final screen looks unfinished on desktop.
findings.recommendation: Decide one measure for the done page's content and apply it to both cards; let the footer meet the bottom of short pages.

findings.title: 'Back to the slots' link sits flush against the H1
findings.description: On the vehicle step the back link has no space between it and 'Your vehicle and waste', so the two read as one block.
findings.impact: Design note: spacing rhythm breaks at the top of the step.
findings.recommendation: Apply the spacing scale between the back link and the heading.

findings.title: Expired-slot state keeps 'Book this slot' as the primary action
findings.description: When the held slot has expired, the error says 'This slot is no longer available.', the slot row shows '–', yet the filled 'Book this slot' button remains the only primary action; the route back is a small 'Change slot' link in the summary.
findings.impact: Design note: the strongest element on the page asks for an action that cannot succeed.
findings.recommendation: Decide what the primary action is when the hold has lapsed and let the error lead to it.
